title: Comparison of two ring clocks: joint readings, rates and environment coupling

key_results.statement: Propagator of a minimal ring clock: $\langle m'\vert e^{-iC_K\mu}\vert m\rangle=u_N(m'-m-\mu/\lambda_0)$, $u_N(y)=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi iky/N}$, $\lvert u_N\rvert^2=P_N(y)=\sin^2(\pi y)/(N^2\sin^2(\pi y/N))$.
$P_N(y)=1$ iff $y\in N\mathbb Z$: a clock started at $\lvert m\rangle$ has a certain reading at $\mu$ iff $\mu/\lambda_0=n\in\mathbb Z$, with reading $m+n \bmod N$.
Two free clocks have independent readings: $p(m_1,m_2;\lambda)=P_{N_1}(m_1-\lambda/\lambda_{01})\,P_{N_2}(m_2-\lambda/\lambda_{02})$.
Rate ratio $\rho:=\lambda_{01}/\lambda_{02}$, so that $x_2=\rho x_1$ with $x_i=\lambda/\lambda_{0i}$.
For $\rho=p/q$ (coprime), both readings are certain exactly on $\Lambda_{12}=\{j\lambda_c: j\ge1\}$, $\lambda_c=q\lambda_{01}=p\lambda_{02}$, with readings $(jq \bmod N_1,\ jp \bmod N_2)$.

The most probable reading of $K_2$ at $\lambda=n\lambda_{01}$ is the integer nearest to $n\rho$ mod $N_2$ (both $n\rho\pm\frac12$ if $n\rho\in\mathbb Z+\frac12$), with probability $P_{N_2}(\delta_n)$, $\delta_n$ the distance of $n\rho$ to $\mathbb Z$.
$\min_\lambda P_==(N^2+2)/(3N^2)$ at $\lambda\in\lambda_0(\mathbb Z+\frac12)$, and $P_=(\lambda)=1$ iff $\lambda\in\lambda_0\mathbb Z$.
The offset $m_2-m_1$ mod $N$ is reproduced with probability $P_=(\lambda-\lambda_s)$, equal to $1$ iff $\lambda\in\lambda_s+\lambda_0\mathbb Z_{>0}$.
For the start $\lvert0\rangle\otimes\lvert b\rangle$, $V_{K_1}(\lambda)=e^{-iC_b\lambda}\lvert0\rangle\langle0\rvert e^{iC_b\lambda}$ with $C_b=C_{K_1}+bA$.
$K_1$ is self-driven in the sense of 02-clock iff $B=0$ or $A\in\mathbb R\,\mathbb 1$.
$C_{K_1}+bA$ is a minimal ring clock contract for every $b\in\mathfrak B$ iff $A=\gamma C_{K_1}$ with $\gamma\in\mathbb R$ and $1+\gamma b>0$ on $\mathfrak B$.
The tick in the environment eigenvalue $b$ is $\lambda_{01}(b)=\lambda_{01}/(1+\gamma b)$.
Two clocks in a common environment have rate ratio $\rho(b)=\rho\,(1+\gamma_2b)/(1+\gamma_1b)$.
$\rho(b)$ is the same for all $b\in\mathfrak B$ iff $\gamma_1=\gamma_2$, and then $\rho(b)=\rho$.

definitions.name: Fejér-type kernel of a ring clock
effective clock contract in environment eigenvalue b
coupling strength of a clock to the environment

open_issues: Readings take values in Z_N, so the advances jq, jp and the nearest integer to nρ are known only modulo N_i; recovering ρ itself needs a count of turns, not derived.
The statistics of a sequence of joint readings of two different clocks is not derived.

Environment states that superpose eigenvectors of B are out of scope; then K_1 can become entangled with E and its view can be mixed (it stays pure, e.g., for A ∈ ℝ·1); when it is mixed is not derived.
Choosing reading values of λ and comparing readings at equal λ uses the order of λ (A8), criterion 8; the meaning of γ_1 = γ_2 for criteria 4–6 is not addressed.

consistency_checks.check: N = 2: coincidence probability 1 − (1/2) sin²(πx), minimum 1/2, two maximal places with probability 1/2 at half-integer nρ
λ_01 = λ_02 (ρ = 1): λ_c = λ_01, K_2 certain at every certain reading of K_1, coincidence probability 1 exactly there
Dimensions and b = 0: γb dimensionless, ticks and ratio reduce to λ_01 and ρ; γ = 0 gives self-drivenness
